svg.title: Pro Micro + SSD1306: component connection guide
svg.desc: Top-view vector components with individually colored wires and named Pro Micro terminals. Display and button connections come from the ArduCade hardware profile. The battery holder, switch and 10 kiloohm resistor are shown as unconnected reference components until their specifications are known.

g.text: ArduCade · SPI · 5 V / 16 MHz · components viewed from above
Wires end at named Pro Micro pins. Matching pin names mean the same connection.
Find the pins on your board; the USB connector may vary.
The board on the left shows
USB type does not indicate 3.3 V / 5 V.
Connect wires to these named pins on the Pro Micro.
Pin order varies between display modules.
The reference has 6 pins, with no visible CS. Verify SPI mode
and the CS connection before using this profile.
The display module must accept 5 V power and signals.
Each button connects one input to GND when pressed.
Internal pull-ups are enabled. No extra button resistors.
Separate circuits: OLED RES is not the board RST.
Appearance alone does not identify active / passive buzzers.
Reference components · not connected in this diagram
Series: about 6 V. Parallel: about 3 V.
Never connect 6 V directly to VCC.
No buzzer resistor value has been selected.
Pro Micro normally has a reset pull-up.
Typical components, not to scale. Follow the pin labels and datasheets for your own modules.
